utterances.text: On occasions they may have been, but generally speaking the blocking of the convoys was done for other reasons, strategic reasons, in order to either lever the Bosnian government into a position or the United Nations forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was this view that you've just expressed shared by other UN officials with whom you were engaged?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL ROSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the universal view.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we see, please, 65 ter 22981 in that regard. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Here we see, General, a letter from Mr. Akashi to Dr. Karadzic dated 30 July 1994 reporting on, among other things, confiscation of sleeping bags, glue for shoe repair, and the damage to 500 bags of wheat, noting that he cannot accept explanations that this was necessary for security reasons. Please have a look at the document and let us know when you're done.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL ROSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Is this -- when you noted that colleagues within the United Nations held this view as universal, is this an example of one of those instances?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL ROSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was typical of the sort of thing that was happening all the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could this be the next Prosecution exhibit, please, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P1686.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, yesterday at page 7455, lines 3 to 20, Dr. Karadzic showed you a document which he said was written to Ambassador Akashi or to Mr. Akashi a day after you took up your duties. And he quoted a passage from this document. It refer -- it was a letter. Referring to a meeting (redacted), just before you arrived on the ground, where he offered to widen the land corridor for the flow of humanitarian aid from Belgrade to Tuzla. And he asked you whether you agreed that this was a fair humanitarian offer, and you agreed. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL ROSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: To put -- I'd like to put that letter in context, and to do so I'd like to call up the actual notes of that meeting but due to the

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: document not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll do so. Private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we are now in open session, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: At page -- oh, I've done my number thing again. I think it's 7562, line 24, to 7564, line 5, Dr. Karadzic put to you a copy of a letter he wrote to Mr. Akashi on 24 June 1992 in response to Mr. Akashi's letter dated the previous day. And that letter -- in that letter, Dr. Karadzic noted: "UNPROFOR forces take little notice of the agreed procedure, for example, undeclared goods and equipment and display unacceptable behaviour as if they're an army of occupation." And he asked Mr. Akashi to use his influence to change the UN's manner of action. Do you remember seeing that document?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL ROSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'd like to show you now Mr. Akashi's letter to Dr. Karadzic of 23 June 1994. It's 65 ter number 22976. And just to further refresh your memory with regards to your previous evidence, you indicated that had you seen the document you would have taken grave exception to it and Akashi would have done the same. There was no case ever of the United Nations allowing its positions to be used by any of the warring parties to prosecute the war. Now you see Dr. Akashi's letter and I'd like to direct your attention in particular to the last paragraph of this document, but please let us know when you've had a look through it.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL ROSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, this last paragraph in particular cites unacceptable delays imposed on the movement of UN convoys and restrictions on the days when such convoys move. Now, did the document shown to you by Dr. Karadzic address to your recall in any regard Mr. Akashi's concerns as regards freedom of movement?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL ROSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we tender this as the next Prosecution exhibit, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P1688, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How much longer do you have, Ms. Edgerton?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I could try for five minutes or less, Your Honour. I'll move with alacrity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have to rise before five, so could you do your best.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: At 7489, line 16, to 7490, line 9, Dr. Karadzic showed you a letter he wrote to Mr. Akashi on 5 September responding to one he had received where Dr. Karadzic said Mr. Akashi mentioned some parts of his speech out of context. Now, I'd like to show you the extract which provoked Mr. Akashi's correspondence to Dr. Karadzic. It's 65 ter 10707. It's a letter to Mr. Akashi from Viktor Andreev.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we go to the second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: This letter, General, attached a statement -- this letter attached an extract of a speech from Dr. Karadzic directing it to Mr. Akashi's attention and it contains the following reference. I think if you look down to the second indented paragraph on this page you would see it. It reads: "Nobody in the world has expected nor protested against economic sanctions that Yugoslavia imposed on the RS. Therefore, we will impose sanctions against Muslims so toughly that a bird could not pass through. These sanctions will last until the world do not force Yugoslavia to lift the sanctions against the RS ..." And my question to you is: In terms of freedom of movement from this period of time, September 1994 until the end of your tour, did you see any manifestations of this increased control like this on the ground?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL ROSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the situation steadily deteriorated throughout the autumn of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could this be the next Prosecution exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P1689, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: That's -- concludes the re-examination, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me, I note we're quick to leave. I was going to ask for a redaction. I can do that if it's possible to do so after we're adjourned or go quickly into private session and give the specific citation. Whatever the Court wishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think you can handle that outside the courtroom. Mr. Karadzic, we have to rise. You can make submissions on Monday.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to put a single question to the General, a very brief question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: About the document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In relation to that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: About your effective control?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then we'll allow you just one question briefly. Further cross-examination by Mr. Karadzic:

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, sir, effective control of the Secretary-General over the United Nations forces in Bosnia-Herzegovina, was that a tactical, operational, or strategic level?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL ROSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would have been exercised at the strategic level.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. That concludes your evidence, General, Sir Michael. I'd like to thank you on behalf of the Bench and Tribunal for coming to The Hague to give it and to assist the Tribunal. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll resume Monday at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 11th day of October, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.06 p.m.,
